MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  February 13, 2024
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:00 p.m., on February 13, 2024, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 8, 2024, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell ~ arrived 5:12pm
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

 CLOSED SESSION

 CS1.  Conference with Legal Counsel – Pending Litigation: Janice Kronik Gath, et. al v.
  Mission Viejo OCSC Case No. 30-2024-01376969-CU-MC-CJC and Initiation of
  Litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 (15 cases)

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Spoke of the CC&R’s that were validated in 2015. She stated that the City
  Attorney and City Council Members have the responsibility to do what is best for the City by obeying
  the law and not breaking it. She criticized the City Attorney on his actions and behavior, and blamed
  the City Manager for the City’s violation of the CC&R’s, and impending lawsuit. She reiterated the
  City Council should perform within the boundaries of the law, that the CC&R’s are in place to protect
  all prop owners, and to not allow the City Attorney to build up significant costs again.

City Council Minutes  1  February 13, 2024
   RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

  At the hour of 5:00pm Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. Mayor Kelley
  reconvened the meeting at 6:03pm with all five Council Members present.

 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

 City Attorney Bill Curley stated the City Council received an update on CS1, and gave direction as to
 defending the City. No reportable specifics.

 INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

 PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Bucknum

 PRESENTATIONS

 P1.  Recognize the Mission Viejo High School Football Team on Their CIF State Division 1-
  AA Championship

  Mayor Kelley presented commendations.

 Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Congratulated the Diablos Football Team on an exciting season. Thanked the
 fans, cheerleaders, band, and families, as they are a vital part of game. She stated this year was a roller-
 coaster but the team worked hard, challenged each other to be better, had an epic season and won the
 trophy. She concluded by stating she is looking forward to a repeat in 2024.

 PUBLIC COMMENTS

 Gayle Wood, M.V.: Chairperson of the Marines and Sailors Adoption Committee, thanked the City
 Council for their support of the brave men and women of the Headquarters Battalion First Division at
 Camp Pendleton, and the Marine Adoption Committee. She also gave a big thank you to the residents
 of Mission Viejo for their generosity and support of the 190 families, which they adopted, over the
 holidays. She concluded, that due to the volume of toys donated by Mission Viejo residents, the
 Committee was able to help out two other battalions at Camp Pendleton.

 Valentina Naranjo, M.V.: President of Community of Character Committee, spoke of opportunities,
 leadership qualities, and volunteer programs within the Committee for students between 7th grade and
 high school. She explained how each month of the year represents a character word/ trait, and spoke
 of the importance of this month’s word ~ Unity. She concluded with a quote from Mother Theresa.

 Walt Lawson, M.V.: Spoke of making Mission Viejo greener, benefiting all residents and combating
 air pollution. He questions why the City did not purchase electric vehicles last year, he gave a couple
 of suggestions with regards to developing action plans, and mentioned Federal and State incentives
 for purchasing electric vehicles. Lastly, he asked who on the dais owns an electric car.

City Council Minutes  2  February 13, 2024
  Ed Maurer, M.V.: Spoke of today’s exciting video presentation, and previous videos of Mayor Goodell
 during his trips related to the 2028 LA Olympics. He is hopefully Mayor Kelley will provide a video
 at the end of this year, and suggested she give an update on the efforts made to reduce the City’s
 Greenhouse Gas Emissions/Climate Action Plan.

 Shane Ingalls, M.V.: Referred to the proposal he sent to the City Council with regards to converting
 Cordillera Elementary School into a public park. He appreciated the feedback he received, however,
 he wanted to highlight a few of the benefits in person.

 Mayor Kelley requested staff provide an overview pertaining to Mr. Maurer’s comments at a future
 council meeting, and also an update from staff on Cordillera Elementary School.

City Council Minutes  4  February 13, 2024
  CITY MANAGER REPORTS

 City Manager Wilberg shared that the State Department of Housing and Community Development
 finally certified the City’s Housing Element. He wished Cathy Palmer was here to hear the outcome,
 as she was very interested in the process and provided a lot of comments, and hopefully appreciates
 the hard work and that the City finally reached the finish line. He also added, that he has a meeting
 scheduled with Superintendent Turner next week and Cordillera Elementary School is just one of the
 items he shall be discussing with her.

 Mayor Kelley congratulated and thanked Director Lister and her staff for the arduous task in preparing
 the Housing Element and all their hard work.

 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

 16.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

 Council Member Bucknum

 Council Member Bucknum commenced by asking when the Housing Element was submitted to the
 State, and City Manager Wilberg responded October 2021. She also mentioned it would be beneficial
 to know the cost to the City. She stated that food/taco/fruit carts are popping up on the streets in
 Mission Viejo and taking business away from existing businesses. She implored residents to support
 brick and mortar shops, and mentioned the Rubio’s fundraiser taking place on Thursday, February 29,
 giving 30% of proceeds in support of the Marine Adoption Committee. She asked staff, the City
 Attorney and Orange County Sherriff’s Department to investigate how other cities, such as Anaheim
 and Irvine, are handling this and report back to Council at a future meeting. Council Member Bucknum
 also mentioned the danger of Proposition 1 ~ Behavioral Health Services Program and Bond Measure,
 which the Council opposed at the January 23, 2024 meeting. It creates a by-right approval process for
 adult substance use disorder residential program and recovery housing, and if it passed into law will
 allow agencies to put regulations into place with no oversight by voters, and redirect County local
 money. She referred to a factsheet on the City’s website and advised all to review. She attended the
 Mission Viejo Chapter, Daughters of the American Revolution (NSDAR) ~ 40th Anniversary, and the
 Crucero Park Playground Area Rehab Meeting. She thanked City Staff for a great job, and residents
 for their feedback and perspective. Lastly, she reminded everyone of the upcoming events this
 Saturday, February 17, Dump Day, Farmers Market, and in the evening enjoy the Love Fest Night
 Market.

 Council Member Goodell

 Council Member Goodell gave an update on all the exciting things happening with the Sports and
 Economic Tourism Committee. He mentioned he met with an Olympian from Israel today and toured
 the Aquatics facilities, while Director Mark Nix took the Mexican Football Federation on a tour of
 City facilities. Next week a European Contingent shall be touring City facilities, followed by another
City Council Minutes  5  February 13, 2024
  large European Contingent the following month. He concluded by stating there is a lot going on and
 the Committee is working hard to answer all requests put forward to them, and he anticipates it will
 only get busier following the Summer Olympics in Paris this summer.

 Council Member Vasquez

 Council Member Vasquez stated she also attended the 2024 Chamber of Commerce Business Kick
 Off Mixer, at which the Chamber unveiled the MVCC Magazine release ~ a great resource. She
 appreciated being part of Mission Viejo Chapter, Daughters of the American Revolution (NSDAR) ~
 40th Anniversary event. And, last night she attended the Crucero Park Playground Area Rehab
 Meeting. She added, it was nice to see a lot or residents involved and providing input. She thanked
 and congratulated Director Elaine Lister and her staff on the awesome job of completing the housing
 element. She is happy the City finally has a Certified Housing Element. She concluded by adding it
 is now officially Girl Scout Cookie season, plus her daughter is hosting a community clean up at
 9:45am on Saturday, March 2, and invited other Girl Scout Troops to join them.

 Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch

 Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch stated he was absent at last City Council meeting attending a Vector Control
 Seminar, and added that Director Laura Young shall be giving a presentation on Sterile Insect
 Technique (SIT) Program at the upcoming Council Meeting in March. He regularly attends the weekly
 Daybreakers Chamber meetings. Two weeks ago, he attended the Association of California Cities –
 Orange County (ACCOC) dinner and the topic was Artificial intelligence (AI) in Business &
 Government, a very interesting conversation. Lastly, he and his wife had great fun attending the
 Gnome Hunt event at Oso Creek Golf Course. He commended the golf course for all they do, and
 encourage everyone to stop by, if only for coffee.

 Mayor Kelley

 Mayor Kelley announced she attended the 2024 Business Kick Off Mixer put on by the Chamber of
 Commerce, the Daughters of the American Revolution (NSDAR) ~ 40th Anniversary event, and the
 Crucero Park Playground Area Rehab Meeting. Lastly, she encouraged all to visit the Farmers Market
 held every Saturday from 9am-1pm.

ADJOURNMENT AT 7:25 PM TO TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 27, 2024, AT 5:00 P.M.
